newsitem.title: UK: Man cuts east Europe 96/97 sugar output estimate.
newsitem.headline: Man cuts east Europe 96/97 sugar output estimate.

text.p: Lower sugar output in Ukraine, Bulgaria and Belarus should cut eastern Europe's total 1996/97 production by 700,000 tonnes white value to 8.20 million, trade house E D & F Man said in its latest monthly report on Tuesday.
The previous estimate for east European sugar production was 8.50 million tonnes for 1996/97, Man said.
Ukraine was expected to turn out 2.60 million tonnes in 1996/97, 200,000 tonnes less than the previous forecast in October. The revised figure was in line with the latest official estimate, Man said.
Sugar productions in Bulgaria and Belarus were likely to fall from last year, it said.
An official forecast of higher beet production in Russia would result in around 1.70 million tonnes of sugar, in line with Man's earlier estimate and based on similar yields seen last year.
